subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be permanently denied access to legacy ownerless session rows, or should OpenClaw first provide an explicit safe migration or repair path for rows whose owner cannot be inferred?
rationale: The patch changes upgrade-time authorization for persisted sessions. Source evidence supports fail-closed isolation, but only maintainers can choose the permanent compatibility and operator-recovery contract.

options.title: Retain fail-closed legacy behavior
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime access to ownerless rows and leave those rows manageable only through non-plugin/operator paths until a separately designed migration exists.

options.title: Design a migration first
options.body: Pause merge until maintainers define a safe owner-assignment or recovery workflow that does not permit arbitrary plugin adoption.

recommendation.title: Retain fail-closed legacy behavior
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime access to ownerless rows and leave those rows manageable only through non-plugin/operator paths until a separately designed migration exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged ownership of the Gateway session-handler architecture makes this the strongest available routing candidate.
